dedupe_keys.name: spaceports of the world data repository

description: Spaceports of the World is an interactive data repository of the active ground-based spaceports that have supported at least one successful orbital launch, with cumulative launches per spaceport and year from 1957 to 2022 and the orbital regime (LEO, MEO, GEO, other, missing) and inclination of each launch's primary payload. It is produced by the Center for Strategic and International Studies Aerospace Security Project, by Thomas G. Roberts with the CSIS iDeas Lab, to accompany its report on spaceports. Coverage is global, with 28 spaceports used for orbital launch since 1957; air- and sea-launched platforms are excluded. Format and access: an interactive web map and charts on the CSIS site, viewable without registration; no bulk file was seen. Licence: not stated on the page; free to view. Caveats: last updated on 31 January 2023, so newer spaceports and launches are missing, and inactive spaceports appear only in the report. It supports exposure and capacity studies of launch infrastructure. Related catalogue records are GCAT, whose launch sites table covers every launch origin, and Launch Library 2.
